articles.title: Florence Nightingale as a pioneer of applied statistics: Data, visualization, and the foundations of modern healthcare quality improvement.
articles.authorString: Zrelak PA.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Florence Nightingale (1820-1910) is widely recognized as the founder of modern nursing, yet her influence extends into applied statistics, data visualization, and data-driven reform.

Purpose

This conceptual historical analysis reframes Nightingale as an early applied statistician, emphasizing her systematic data collection, analytic reasoning, and innovative graphics to influence health policy and institutional change.

Methods

Drawing on nineteenth-century developments in statistical graphics and her collaboration with William Farr, the article moves beyond the polar area diagram to examine her broader graphical and tabular toolkit. It then considers how her mortality data can be reinterpreted using interrupted time-series methods, comparative dashboards, and modern hospital safety analytics, while noting limitations of nineteenth-century data systems.

Discussion

By linking Nightingale's work to contemporary infection prevention, hospital harm surveillance, and performance dashboards, the analysis positions her as an early architect of data-driven quality improvement.

Conclusion

Nightingale's work underscores nursing's longstanding role in evidence-based leadership and systems reform.

articles.abstractText:
Background

In the United Kingdom, first contact practitioners (FCPs) provide direct access to musculoskeletal (MSK) assessment and management in primary care. This means FCPs have to assess patients with no prior medical screening, which assumes reliance on developed skills and experience. The pool of appropriately experienced physiotherapists is limited, and less experienced clinicians have been recruited. A 2026 national evaluation found substantial variation in FCP service delivery, with data collection and governance among its structural causes. The Primary Care Individual Social Norms MSK Data Dashboard (PRISM) dashboard gives FCPs feedback on their clinical activity relative to their peers to support reflection toward improving MSK care.

Objective

This study aimed to co-design the metrics, filters, and guidance content of the PRISM dashboard and guidebook to reflect evidence-based practice and the real-world context of FCP roles, and apply a critical realist approach to identify the mechanisms and conditions shaping its design.

Methods

This qualitative co-design study used a modified nominal group process across 2 online workshops in June and August 2025, with 10 purposively sampled participants: clinical FCPs, national physiotherapy and data leaders, and a patient representative. Two analytic strands were applied to the same data. The consensus process produced the metric set and filters. Critical realist thematic analysis of the transcripts using NVivo (version 12 Plus; QSR International), with line-by-line coding using inductive and a priori codes, identified the conditions shaping how those metrics would need to be interpreted.

Results

Participants reached consensus on a core metric set describing the breadth of the FCP role, separating variation generated by clinical decisions from variation generated by structure such as local diagnostic access, prescribing rights, and referral pathways. Contextual filters were co-designed at patient, clinician, and service level to keep structure visible. Supervision emerged as a condition surrounding the dashboard rather than a component, since the same comparison prompts reflection where role clarity and psychological safety are present and defensiveness where they are not. A tool dependent on supervision would work least well where support is weakest. This means that an option for stand-alone use is a design requirement. Three data integrity risks were identified: recording reliability, data gaming, and clinician burden. The guidebook enables these conditions to be transferred into practice, with separate guidance for FCPs and supervisors and a 4-step reflection structure.

Conclusions

Expert co-design produced a metric set describing the breadth of the role while accommodating variation between services and acknowledging the conditions under which PRISM can function as intended. This paper moves from the national position that FCP services collect data to a specification of the conditions under which collecting data produces learning. Mapping of the metrics against National Institute for Health and Care Excellence MSK guidelines and quality indicators is reported in a companion paper.

articles.abstractText: This study evaluates the impact of implementing a real-time intrapartum digital monitoring dashboard on labor progression and birth outcomes in a high-resource high-volume tertiary care delivery ward. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a university-affiliated medical center. We included all women admitted for an attempted vaginal delivery between January 2012 and December 2022. The intervention group included deliveries from January 2021 to December 2022, after full implementation of the dashboard. The control group included deliveries between January 2012 and May 2019, prior to implementation. Deliveries during the system's rollout phase (June 2019 to December 2020) and elective cesarean sections were excluded. The dashboard displayed real-time maternal and fetal data for all delivery rooms simultaneously. The primary outcome was labor duration, measured from admission to the delivery room until delivery. Secondary outcomes included prolonged second stage of labor, intrapartum fever, perineal lacerations (including obstetric anal sphincter injury), vacuum deliveries, and 5-min Apgar score < 7. Multivariable logistic regression and trend analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders. A total of 90 530 women were included in the study (70 922 pre-implementation and 19 608 post-implementation). After adjusting for maternal and clinical characteristics, dashboard implementation was associated with lower risk of labor >6 h (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0.67, 95% CI 0.6-0.7) and prolonged second stage (aRR 0.64, 95% CI 0.5-0.7) and with fewer perineal lacerations (aRR 0.80, 95% CI 0.7-0.9). There were no significant differences in vacuum delivery rates or adverse neonatal outcomes. Implementation of a real-time digital dashboard for intrapartum monitoring was associated with shorter labor and fewer perineal injuries without compromising neonatal safety, supporting a potential role for ward-wide digital monitoring in intrapartum care.

articles.title: Wound3DAssist: A Practical Framework for 3D Wound Assessment.
articles.authorString: Chierchia R, Cruz RS, Lebrat L, Arzhaeva Y, Armin MA, Oorloff J, Nguyen C, Salvado O, Fookes C, Ahmedt-Aristizabal D.

journal.title: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

articles.abstractText: Managing chronic wounds remains a major healthcare challenge, with clinical assessment often relying on subjective and time-consuming manual documentation methods. Although 2D digital videometry frameworks have aided wound measurement, these approaches struggle with perspective distortion, a limited field of view, and an inability to capture wound depth, especially in anatomically complex or curved regions. To overcome these limitations, we present Wound3DAssist, a practical framework for 3D wound assessment using monocular consumer-grade videos. Our framework generates 3D wound models from short handheld recordings captured using consumer-grade devices, enabling non-contact, automatic measurements from reconstructed multi-view surfaces. We integrate 3D reconstruction, wound segmentation, tissue classification, and periwound analysis into a modular workflow. We evaluate Wound3DAssist across digital models with known geometry, silicone phantoms, and real patients. Results show that the framework supports high-quality wound bed visualization, approximately millimeter-scale surface reconstruction accuracy in the evaluated clinical cases, and multi-view wound-tissue composition analysis. Full assessments are completed in under 20 minutes, demonstrating feasibility for a research framework intended for future clinical workflow evaluation.

articles.abstractText:
Introduction

The epidemiology of breast cancer among men is poorly characterized. As the Veterans Health Administration (VA) serves a disproportionally male population, a larger percentage of breast cancer cases diagnosed and treated in VA are among male patients. However, whether current breast oncology operational infrastructure is prepared to address this need is unclear.

Materials and methods

The VA Breast and Gynecologic Oncology System of Excellence (BGSoE) established a tracking dashboard for all incident breast and gynecologic malignancies in VA in 2021. All breast surgery cases within the VA performed on male Veterans for an indication of cancer in 2023 were reviewed and mapped by the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN). Operative cases performed for gynecomastia were excluded. To determine the total affected population, incidence of male breast cancer was calculated using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Breast surgeries, reported as a fraction of incident cases, were plotted. The number of active surgeons performing breast surgery in 2023 was garnered from the staff surgeon identified in the BGSoE dashboard.

Results

Based upon SEER age-adjusted estimates of breast cancer in men nationally and current Veteran census data, there were estimated to be 188 incident cases of breast cancer among male Veterans in 2023. In comparison, 82 (44%) male Veterans underwent surgery for their breast cancers in VA in 2023. The median age of the cohort was 72 years (interquartile range 58-78). Geographic variability in surgical volume was noted, with the number of surgeries performed in each VISN ranging from 0 to 13 cases. VISNs performed between 0% and 112% of the expected number of cancer operations for male Veterans. All VISNs had at least 1 surgeon performing breast surgery among this population in 2023 (range: 1-15).

Conclusions

There is wide variation in incident cases of breast cancer among male Veterans treated in VA. Whether these geographic differences are reflective of differential incidence, discrepancies in access, or availability of breast oncology health services is unclear. Although most patients with breast cancer do present with resectable disease, the proportion of incident cases among male Veterans by our estimates with stage IV disease (not amenable to surgery) cannot be ascertained. Future work will be aimed at characterizing availability of multidisciplinary breast cancer care in VA.

articles.abstractText:
Background

As digital communication becomes central to daily life, psychotherapy increasingly has access to patients' electronic media data. Although digital phenotyping has been widely studied, less is known about whether incorporating personal communication data, such as text messages, improves clinical outcomes in psychotherapy.

Objective

This study aimed to determine whether integrating personalized text message data into psychotherapy improves depression, anxiety, health-related quality of life, and therapeutic alliance and to examine whether increased access to collateral information influences clinical decision-making.

Methods

The Electronic Media and its Impact on Psychotherapy (EMAP) study was a randomized controlled trial conducted in adult and geriatric outpatient and partial hospitalization settings at an academic psychiatric hospital. Participants receiving psychotherapy for primary depression or anxiety (n=101) were randomized to electronic media-enhanced therapy (EME; n=52) or treatment as usual (TAU; n=49). In EME, research staff reviewed participants' text messages prior to sessions using personalized mood-related key terms and presented aggregated findings on a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)-compliant clinician dashboard. TAU participants received standard care without message review. Outcomes included change scores for the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and the Working Alliance Inventory-Short Revised (WAI-SR). Linear regression and nonparametric tests compared groups. Moderation analyses assessed whether the frequency of information access influenced treatment changes.

Results

No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in anxiety or working alliance. Among participants with SF-36 follow-up data (n=65), EME participants demonstrated greater improvement in the pain subscale. Greater frequency of information access was associated with increased treatment-related changes in the EME group. Access to additional collateral information was associated with more clinical actions but not with improved distal outcomes.

Conclusions

Integrating personalized text message data into short-term psychotherapy did not significantly improve depression or anxiety, and it neither improved nor worsened therapeutic alliance. However, access to greater amounts of collateral information, including electronic media, influenced clinical decision-making, suggesting nuanced and context-dependent effects.

articles.abstractText: This paper describes lessons learned from a partnership between the First Nations Health and Social Secretariat of Manitoba (FNHSSM) and researchers at the University of Manitoba to develop a community-led COVID-19 modelling platform. The envisioned tool would allow First Nations leaders to input local data and generate outputs to support decision-making using a stochastic, age-stratified agent-based model of COVID-19 transmission. Although the platform was not fully operationalized during the project, several important lessons emerged. First, the COVID-19 pandemic placed significant demands on human resources, making such an ambitious initiative difficult to implement during an active public health emergency. Second, the project required coordination among multiple teams with distinct expertise, including model developers, dashboard designers, and FNHSSM information technology staff responsible for infrastructure planning. Competing pandemic-related priorities frequently delayed collaboration and implementation. Third, access to administrative data through the Manitoba Centre for Health Policy involved a six-month reporting lag, limiting the availability of timely information needed for emergency response and decision-making. These challenges highlight structural barriers to data-driven pandemic management in First Nations communities. We recommend: (1) providing First Nations organizations and communities with ongoing access to their own administrative data for service delivery, planning, and emergency management; and (2) establishing First Nations-led data centres with sustainable infrastructure and core funding to support data sovereignty, agile reporting, and future public health response efforts.

articles.abstractText: Methanogenic archaea are an underexplored yet functionally significant component of the human oral microbiota, implicated in eubiosis and dysbiosis, periodontal disease, peri-implantitis, endodontic infections and other systemic diseases. Their low abundance, unique cell wall structures and limited taxonomic markers have historically hampered their detection and visualization. These methodological limitations have contributed to an incomplete understanding of their spatial organization and potential roles in oral health and disease. Recent advances in microscopy and molecular imaging have transformed our ability to study these microorganisms in situ, providing increasingly detailed spatial, structural and functional information. This review synthesizes established and emerging imaging approaches for oral methanogenic archaea, spanning rapid low-resolution detection, molecularly targeted imaging, ultrastructural and nanoscale characterization and emerging label-free and functional methods. We critically compare these approaches according to their taxonomic specificity, spatial resolution, quantitative capability, sample-preparation constraints and current level of validation for oral methanogens. Emphasis is placed on biological insights gained, including spatial organization within biofilms, interspecies interactions and potential functional roles in oral health and disease. Key gaps remain, including the need for standardized imaging protocols, real-time in situ visualization and quantitative methods suitable for clinical translation. To address these challenges, we propose an integrative framework combining tiered imaging modalities to guide experimental design and interpretation. By distinguishing established applications from translational and extrapolative approaches, this review provides a methodological roadmap for future imaging studies of oral methanogens and highlights priorities for their rigorous investigation in dental research.

articles.abstractText: Arrhythmia poses a serious threat to human health, necessitating research into automated diagnostic methods. Although advances have been made in arrhythmia classification using deep learning, existing models often suffer from high computational cost and poor interpretability, limiting their clinical applicability. To this end, this paper proposes a lightweight progressive residual convolutional attention network (DResCA). Through the synergistic design of stage-adaptive downsampling and channel attention, this network reduces parameter redundancy while enhancing deep ECG feature extraction. To enhance clinical interpretability, template matching and attention visualization are employed to reveal the key ECG regions underlying the model's diagnoses. Five-class classification experiments on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the model achieves 98.35% accuracy and 97.99% macro-F1 score while maintaining fewer parameters than mainstream deep learning models. These characteristics provide a practical technical pathway for real-time arrhythmia detection on wearable edge computing devices.

articles.authorString: Elvis Akem T.

articles.abstractText: The second WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for mpox was declared on 14 August 2024 after clade Ib monkeypox virus emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and spread rapidly across Africa and internationally. The PHEIC ended on 5 September 2025, and the Africa CDC Public Health Emergency of Continental Security was lifted on 22 January 2026. This study characterised global and Africa-specific mpox epidemiology across the full second PHEIC cycle and immediate post-emergency period, from January 2024 to February 2026. A retrospective surveillance analysis was conducted using the WHO Global Mpox Trends dashboard exported data, supplemented by WHO situation reports S32-S64 and international and national surveillance reports. Analyses included negative binomial segmented regression, travel-linked pathway analysis, exploratory analysis of documented secondary transmission after travel-linked detection, and descriptive statistics. Models used reported case counts with log population offsets; reported case-rate ratios therefore reflect reported case rates rather than true infection incidence. Between January 2024 and February 2026, 82,738 confirmed cases and 306 deaths were reported to WHO globally (case fatality ratio 0.37%). The PHEIC period accounted for 74.0% of cases, peaking at 7,405 cases in May 2025. In total, 163 clade-specific importation or travel-linked detection events were documented across 41 countries within the primary analytic cutoff; documented secondary transmission occurred in 25 (15.3%) events across 16 countries. Within DRC, 200 health zones recorded 144,035 total reported cases and 2,047 deaths (case fatality ratio 1.42%); these aggregate suspected/clinically compatible and confirmed cases. The top 20 health zones accounted for 45.4% of national burden. Reported transmission declined after the May 2025 peak but persisted beyond PHEIC termination. Emergency termination marked an administrative transition, not the end of mpox transmission. The post-emergency period requires sustained surveillance, maintained diagnostic capacity, targeted response in persistent transmission settings, and equitable access to vaccines and countermeasures.

articles.abstractText:
Background

This study aimed to compare intraoperative visualization between diluted epinephrine (EPN) irrigation and preoperative intravenous tranexamic acid (TXA) during the glenohumeral and subacromial phases of rotator cuff repair.

Methods

Eighty-two patients with rotator cuff tears were prospectively randomized (1:1) to receive either 0.33 mg/L EPN irrigation without TXA (EPN group) or preoperative intravenous TXA (15 mg/kg) without EPN irrigation (TXA group). Visual clarity was evaluated using a pretrained deep learning model with a 3-point grading scale across three stages: intra-articular assessment, subacromial debridement, and rotator cuff repair. Irrigation pump pressure was recorded at each stage. Hypotensive bradycardic events (HBEs) and postoperative adverse events were monitored.

Results

Overall visual clarity was significantly greater in the EPN group than in the TXA group (mean difference [MD], 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.10; P<0.001). Visualization was superior with EPN during subacromial debridement (MD, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.03-0.13; P=0.001) and rotator cuff repair (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.004-0.06; P=0.02). The EPN group required lower pump pressures and fewer increases in pressure. No significant differences in HBEs or adverse events were observed.

Conclusions

articles.abstractText:
Objective

Ankle sprains often involve injury to the lateral fibulotalocalcaneal ligament complex (LFTCL). The LFTCL consists of the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL), the calcaneofibular ligament (CFL), and connecting fibers (CoFi) connecting the ATFL and CFL. Technical advancements in 3D MRI imaging enable the identification of the LFTCL and CoFi. This report aims to define the optimal imaging planes for morphology assessment of the CoFi using 3D MRI sequences.

Materials and methods

The current report included a pilot of five MRI scans. In all patients 3D proton density MRI sequences were acquired using isotropic voxels of 0.52 mm. Selected patients had no relevant ankle pathology. The LFTCL was identified, and optimal imaging planes were assessed in axial and sagittal views, relative to the predefined neutral axis. Scan planes with the least number of slices (median) needed for complete visualization of the CoFi were defined as the optimal imaging planes. Anatomical features of the CoFi were evaluated, including signal intensity, continuity, bundle count, shape, orientation, length, and intrinsic angle.

Results

In all 5 patients, CoFi was present. The axial optimal plane was a 25° scan angle tilted cranially relative to the neutral axis. The sagittal optimal plane was a 0° scan angle relative to the neutral axis. The CoFi consisted of one or two bundles, which were all continuous, mostly arciform, and ventrocranially oriented. The length of the CoFi ranged from 40.5 to 45.8 mm in the axial plane. The intrinsic angle of the CoFi ranged from 124.6 to 155.0° in the sagittal plane.

Conclusion

The optimal imaging planes identified in this report allow complete visualization of the CoFi of the LFTCL using 3D MRI techniques. Knowledge of the localization and shape of the CoFi is important in patients presenting with LFTCL injury, as it enables complete assessment of continuity. Future studies including more patients are needed to define clinical importance in patients with isolated CoFi injury and complete LFTCL injury and the role of CoFi in unsuccessful conservative and surgical treatment after LFTCL injury.

articles.abstractText: The use of medical real-world data is constrained by fragmented data infrastructures and the absence of tools integrating longitudinal clinical with molecular data at scale. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), the most common monogenic cause of kidney failure, exemplifies this gap given its phenotypic complexity and the need for individualized treatment decisions. We present MEDA-PKD (MEdical DAta translation service of Polycystic Kidney Disease), an interactive, near-real-time analytics platform that integrates clinical routine with research data from the German AD(H)PKD Tolvaptan Registry (NCT02497521, DRKS00008910) into a harmonized database ( https://doi.org/10.18716/adpkd_registry ). MEDA-PKD provides automated near-real-time analysis and dynamic visualization, replacing traditional static approaches to clinical cohorts. As of March 2026, MEDA-PKD visualized data from 1735 patients (mean follow-up 796 days). eGFR slope analysis of data from patients initiating tolvaptan therapy (332 patients) demonstrates the platform's capacity to evaluate real-world therapeutic impact in real-time. Other tabs include family history, medication, lifestyle, quality of life and a wide array of lab values (20,894 entries). Besides, MEDA-PKD integrates proteomics data and allows for secure individual patient-level data access. MEDA-PKD represents a paradigm shift by transforming static cohort data into a living, actionable knowledge resource in ADPKD and will serve as a template for other diseases.

articles.abstractText:
Unlabelled

Urology education must prepare learners to integrate anatomical visualization, diagnostic reasoning, technical performance, communication, and ethical judgment, often under restricted working hours and limited access to high-fidelity cases. This viewpoint argues that large language models (LLMs) and metaverse-related technologies should be integrated as complementary, supervised educational tools rather than treated as autonomous replacements for educators or clinical experience. LLMs can support cognitive apprenticeship, documentation practice, assessment, and communication simulations, whereas extended reality, cloud computing, and virtual digital humans can support spatial, procedural, and remote learning. Our aim is to articulate 3 key messages: first, the educational value of these technologies depends on alignment with defined urological competencies; second, implementation should proceed in stages from governed data infrastructure to intelligent interaction and immersive multimodal training; and third, educational effectiveness must be established through prospective evaluations of transfer to clinical performance, not through technical novelty alone. We emphasize the need for rigorous randomized controlled trials, identify requirements for haptic and biomechanical fidelity, and discuss hallucination, bias, privacy, accountability, and deskilling. The responsible future of intelligent urology education will therefore require collaboration among learners, educators, clinicians, engineers, ethicists, institutions, and professional bodies.

articles.abstractText: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein families (containing ⪰100 members) derived from over 105 million predicted proteins. Each protein family is enriched with multi-layered annotations, including AlphaFold3 structural predictions, taxonomic classifications, and biome-specific metadata. To further expand their functional annotation, we integrated deep genomic context analysis to link protein families to mobile genetic elements, biosynthetic gene clusters, antibiotic resistance genes, and CRISPR elements. Accessible through the EnvoFams portal, WasteFams provides a user-friendly interface featuring advanced search capabilities, sequence and structural similarity tools, and interactive visualization modules. As global initiatives increasingly leverage wastewater for public health and environmental insights, WasteFams can serve as a critical resource for discovering novel microbial functions, monitoring resistance mechanisms, and exploring the biotechnological potential of secondary metabolites within wastewater-engineered ecosystems.

articles.abstractText: Neuro-point-of-care ultrasound (NeuroPOCUS) is an emerging bedside modality that extends the neurological examination through real-time assessment of cerebral structure and hemodynamics in neurocritical care. Despite increasing integration into clinical pathways and endorsement of transcranial ultrasound-based neuromonitoring by international guidelines, implementation is often hampered by inadequate acoustic windows and poor image and Doppler signal quality, frequently leading to nondiagnostic examinations. Ultrasound contrast agents (UCAs), traditionally used in specialist neurosonology, may overcome these barriers and recover diagnostic information in patients with limited acoustic windows. This clinically oriented narrative review synthesizes the available evidence on contrast-enhanced transcranial ultrasound and examines its potential translation into NeuroPOCUS as a bedside tool for frontline clinicians across vasospasm monitoring, intracranial pressure assessment, evaluation of steno-occlusive cerebrovascular disease, assessment of cerebral circulatory arrest, and other neurocritical care applications. A literature search of PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus was conducted through June 2026, and relevant studies, reviews, and guideline documents were descriptively synthesized according to clinical application. Available evidence indicates that UCAs improve Doppler signal quality, enhance visualization of intracranial vessels, and increase the proportion of diagnostic examinations in patients with limited acoustic windows, thereby improving the interpretability of bedside hemodynamic assessments. However, implementation remains constrained by operator dependence, heterogeneous acquisition and interpretation protocols, limited standardization, and the need for structured training and validated, application-specific velocity cutoffs. Looking ahead, contrast enhancement may expand the scope of bedside neurovascular assessment, including in emergency and acute-care settings where dedicated probes and presets are not readily available. Its favorable safety profile and enhanced bedside feasibility may help bridge the gap between guideline recommendations and clinical practice, although further technical and clinical validation is needed to define its role in frontline NeuroPOCUS.

articles.abstractText: Cell death is essential for maintaining health and development of an organism. Although cell death is not inherently detrimental, processes such as apoptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis are accompanied by significant alterations in the intracellular microenvironment, including changes in pH and viscosity. However, the simultaneous monitoring of pH and viscosity remains challenging and has not yet been demonstrated in Drosophila melanogaster (Dm) third-instar larvae, a physiologically relevant model of developmentally programmed starvation-induced autophagy. Herein, we report PSM-NAP-OH, a dual-responsive fluorescent probe capable of ratiometric pH sensing and turn-on viscosity response. The probe integrates a dihydroxy-functionalized pentacyclic pyridinium framework for ratiometric pH response and a naphthyl rotor as viscosity-sensitive unit through a restricted intramolecular rotation (RIR). It primarily localizes in mitochondria and enables simultaneous monitoring of pH and viscosity changes during apoptosis, ferroptosis, and autophagy in living cells, as well as during autophagy in Dm third-instar larval tissues. Confocal fluorescence imaging studies revealed distinct pH and viscosity profiles for different cell death pathways. Notably, this work represents the first demonstration of simultaneous visualization of pH and viscosity alterations associated with developmentally programmed starvation-induced autophagy in the fat tissue of Dm larvae. These findings establish pH and viscosity as complementary biomarkers of autophagy and provide a new platform for investigating dynamic microenvironmental changes during development and disease.

articles.abstractText:
Introduction

Lumbar neural compression is one of the leading causes of pain and disability in older adults. Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic (UBE) decompression has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to conventional techniques, providing a wider surgical field, enhanced visualization, and preservation of anatomical structures.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients with lumbar spinal stenosis who underwent decompression using the UBE technique between January 2022 and January 2024. Demographic data, surgical details, and clinical and functional outcomes were analyzed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), length of hospital stay, and medical leave duration.

Results

A total of 98 patients were included, with a mean age of 65 ±10 years and a predominance of females. Mean VAS scores decreased from 8.0 ±1.0 preoperatively to 4.0 ±1.0 postoperatively (p < 0.001), while ODI scores improved from 50 ±10 to 20 ±5 (p < 0.001). Purpose

This technical procedure describes a tablet-based augmented reality (AR) workflow for prosthetically driven single-implant placement using tooth-supported marker registration and postoperative planned-to-placed three-dimensional (3D) verification.

Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), intraoral scans, and digital wax-up data were integrated to generate a prosthetically driven implant plan. The planning dataset was converted into an AR-compatible model and visualized on a tablet using the TreLab software. A tooth-supported AR marker guide was fabricated for marker-based registration. During surgery, the surgeon intermittently consulted the AR overlay as a visual reference to the planned implant axis and contextual anatomy. The drill was not tracked, and the osteotomy depth and implant placement were conventionally controlled. Postoperative CBCT was performed, and planned-to-placed deviations were calculated by best-fit superimposition using the remaining teeth as the reference region.

The workflow was completed without intraoperative complications or technical interruptions. Planned-to-placed verification demonstrated an angular deviation of 3.25°, a coronal 3D deviation of 0.68 mm, and an apical 3D deviation of 0.93 mm. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating prosthetically driven implant planning, tablet-based AR visualization, tooth-supported registration, and postoperative planned-to-placed verification into a single-implant clinical workflow. Because neither the drill nor the implant was dynamically tracked and the quantitative overlay error was not measured, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary technical verification rather than as evidence of navigational accuracy or clinical superiority.

articles.abstractText: The integration of ultrasound imaging into preclinical anatomy teaching is often questioned with respect to its objective impact on anatomical knowledge. This study aimed to (i) evaluate short-term knowledge gain following ultrasound-integrated anatomy teaching, (ii) characterize students' perceptions of the learning experience, and (iii) assess the feasibility of delivery across rural, metropolitan, and international settings. Integrated ultrasound sessions were delivered to preclinical medical students in four settings (rural Australian graduate-entry, metropolitan Australian direct-entry, and metropolitan and rural Malaysian direct-entry). Short-term knowledge gain was assessed in the Australian rural cohort using a pretest-posttest design with counterbalanced parallel forms, analyzed with linear mixed-effects models. Student feedback underwent content analysis and feasibility was summarized using key implementation descriptors. In the short-term knowledge gain study (103 students; 193 observed assessments), posttest performance was significantly higher than pretest performance (adjusted mean difference 0.66 correct answers, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.23-1.08; p = 0.003). Students reported benefits for in situ visualization, spatial understanding, and clinical relevance. Delivery was feasible at all four sites, including by videoconference where no local ultrasound unit was available. In conclusion, integrated ultrasound was feasible across diverse settings and, in the Australian rural cohort, was associated with higher assessment performance immediately after teaching. As the design had no parallel comparator, this finding indicates short-term knowledge gain rather than a causal effect or long-term retention. Together, these findings support ultrasound as a complementary preclinical tool, rather than being reserved solely for post-curricular clinical skill acquisition.

articles.abstractText: Reliable identification and early prediction of epileptic seizures play a critical role in improving patient outcomes and supporting timely therapeutic decision-making. To address the challenges of spatiotemporal feature coupling and long-range dependency modeling in multi-channel EEG signals, this paper proposes a channel-adaptive temporal modeling framework named GCNN-Informer. The framework follows a three-stage pipeline: a grouped convolutional network (GCNN) extracts local features and selects the five most discriminative channels; a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) performs dual spatiotemporal enhancement; and a lightweight Informer encoder captures global temporal dependencies via the ProbSparse self-attention mechanism. Experiments on the CHB-MIT dataset, conducted under a patient-specific evaluation scheme, demonstrated that the proposed method achieved accuracies of 97.33% for seizure detection and 97.28% for seizure prediction, with a low false detection rate (FDR) of 0.30/h and a false prediction rate (FPR) of 0.03/h. Grad-CAM visualization further shows that as EEG signals evolve from normal/interictal to preictal and then to ictal stages, the model's attention heatmap progressively transitions from locally sparse highlighting to continuous block-like highlighting, and finally to dense deep-red responses - a pattern that closely aligns with clinical electrophysiological dynamics. This study provides an accurate and generalizable deep-learning solution for real-time epileptic monitoring and early-warning systems.

articles.abstractText: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) is an established treatment for selected pediatric patients with obstructive hydrocephalus. Although the foramen of Monro constitutes the principal anatomical corridor to the third ventricle, its preoperative radiological characterization has been scarcely investigated. This study aimed to describe the radiological characteristics of the foramen of Monro in a consecutive pediatric ETV cohort treated with a small-diameter rigid neuroendoscope and to explore its relationship with ventricular morphology and clinical outcome. A retrospective observational study was performed including the complete consecutive series of 17 pediatric patients who underwent ETV at our institution between March 2022 and November 2024. All procedures were performed using the PaediScope® neuroendoscope. The radiological diameter of the right foramen of Monro was measured on axial T2-weighted MRI together with the Evans Index and third ventricular diameter. Clinical, radiological, and operative variables were retrospectively collected. Correlations between radiological parameters and clinical outcome were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods. The mean radiological diameter of the right foramen of Monro was 2.79 ± 0.81 mm. Moderate positive correlations were observed between the foramen of Monro diameter and the preoperative Evans Index (ρ = 0.588, p = 0.013), preoperative third ventricular diameter (ρ = 0.606, p = 0.010), and postoperative third ventricular diameter (ρ = 0.568, p = 0.017). No significant association was found between the radiological diameter of the foramen of Monro and the subsequent requirement for definitive ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement or postoperative ventricular reduction. Three patients (17.6%) required definitive ventriculoperitoneal shunting during the available clinical follow-up. These patients had significantly lower Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy Success Scores than patients who maintained ETV function (p = 0.016). Intraoperative visualization was good in 16/17 procedures and moderate in one, and no major intraoperative complications were recorded. The radiological measurement of the foramen of Monro correlated with ventricular morphology but was not associated with clinical outcome after pediatric ETV. Rather than representing the true anatomical diameter of the surgical corridor, this measurement should be interpreted as a standardized radiological descriptor of ventricular anatomy. The small diameter neuroendoscope was technically applicable across the range of ventricular anatomy represented in this complete consecutive cohort, although the absence of a comparator precludes conclusions regarding device-specific benefit. The study demonstrates the feasibility of obtaining this measurement from routine preoperative MRI and provides preliminary anatomical data that may support future prospective studies evaluating technical planning for pediatric ventricular endoscopy.

articles.abstractText: Line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT) is an emerging non-invasive imaging technique that provides real-time vertical, horizontal, and three-dimensional visualization of the skin at near-cellular resolution. We systematically reviewed the available evidence on LC-OCT in melanocytic lesions to identify diagnostic features associated with melanoma and to clarify its current clinical role. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026 in accordance with PRISMA recommendations. Thirty-two studies were included, encompassing cutaneous melanoma, lentigo maligna, and facial pigmented lesions, benign and atypical melanocytic lesions, and mucosal melanoma. Across studies, melanoma-associated findings included irregular or disorganized epidermal architecture, numerous or pleomorphic pagetoid cells, disruption or blurring of the dermoepidermal junction, atypical dermal nests, and clefting. In lentigo maligna and facial melanoma, peri-adnexal atypia and follicular involvement emerged as particularly relevant features, whereas mucosal melanoma was characterized by diffuse pagetoid spread, epithelial disarray, atypical junctional cells, and discohesive melanocytic nests. Benign lesions more often showed preserved epidermal architecture, a well-defined junction, organized nests, and a regular wave-like dermal pattern. However, substantial overlap was observed with atypical nevi, spitzoid lesions, blue nevi, melanosis, and other intermediate entities. Although selected studies reported promising diagnostic performance, the evidence remains heterogeneous and is largely based on small, descriptive cohorts. LC-OCT may therefore serve as a useful adjunct in clinically or dermoscopically equivocal melanocytic lesions, but prospective multicenter validation and assessment of reproducibility are required before widespread routine implementation.

articles.abstractText: Clinical ultrasound is widely used because of its low cost, portability, safety, and real-time imaging capability, making it well suited for point-of-care applications. However, conventional B-mode imaging is inherently qualitative and primarily sensitive to tissue morphology. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) methods exploit information contained in backscattered radiofrequency (RF) signals to extract fundamental acoustic tissue properties, such as the backscatter coefficient (BSC) and attenuation, which more directly quantify tissue microstructure and provide complementary information to B-mode imaging. Although QUS methods have been implemented on conventional cart-based ultrasound scanners, their integration into portable handheld systems remains limited. Motivated by the growing availability and clinical potential of ultra-portable ultrasound devices, this protocol presents a QUS imaging pipeline implemented on the DKPOC probe (portable linear ultrasound probe; Vermon SA, Tours, France), which interfaces directly with a laptop through a USB-C connection. The protocol integrates multiple QUS processing methods based on spectral analysis and envelope statistics of RF data acquired using focused-wave or plane-wave transmit modes. QUS processing begins with a user-defined region of interest (ROI). The reference phantom method is used to estimate the BSC and attenuation within sliding sub-ROIs. Model-based fitting of the estimated BSC is then performed to extract tissue microstructure-related parameters, including effective scatterer diameter and effective acoustic concentration. In addition, envelope statistics parameters are estimated using three probability density functions. Computed QUS parameter maps are displayed as translucent color overlays on corresponding B-mode images. The workflow is implemented in a numerical computing software-based graphical user interface, enabling near real-time QUS processing, parameter map visualization, interactive parameter adjustment, and rapid evaluation of different processing configurations. The pipeline is adaptable to different imaging sequences and ultrasound probes, providing a practical framework for quantitative point-of-care ultrasound imaging and clinician-led QUS studies in human subjects.

Objectives

Several variables influence the outcome of cellular assays. We conducted a comprehensive literature review to identify the factors affecting the Monocyte Monolayer Assay (MMA) and subsequently standardized the assay through systematic in-house laboratory trials.

Methods

The study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 involved a literature review using PubMed and Scopus databases to identify factors influencing the assay. Phase 2 included experimental trials to evaluate the effects of these factors. Monocytes were isolated from buffy coat bags, and assay parameters, such as centrifugation speed, monocyte adherence conditions, RBC sensitization, incubation time, and staining, were systematically standardized. A blinded evaluation was employed for slide reading to assess the influence of procedural factors on assay reliability.

Results

A literature review using the PubMed and Scopus databases identified key variables influencing MMA performance. Twelve sequential trials were conducted to identify the effects of these variables on assay outcome. Optimal centrifugation speed and time was 600 × g for 15 min, and the use of four buffy coat bags improved monocyte yield to 8.3 × 106/mL. Dilution with Phosphate buffer saline (PBS, pH 7.2) and use of Histopaque provided consistent cell recovery. A 1-h incubation yielded optimal monocyte adherence with minimal lysis. The final protocol demonstrated high reproducibility and improved visualization of phagocytosis.

Conclusion

This study emphasizes the importance of standardizing the MMA procedure before implementation. Optimizing the parameters to ensure enhanced monocyte yield, reduced cell lysis, and reliable interpretation for assessing the clinical significance of red cell alloantibodies is essential.

articles.abstractText: The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Objectives

Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs.

Methods

This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively.

Results

All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy.

Conclusions

Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact.

Advances in knowledge

This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

Objective

Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes.

Methods

A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC).

Results

Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915.

Conclusion

The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.

articles.abstractText:
Background

Cellular senescence is increasingly recognized as a mechanistic link between cardiovascular ageing, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, and heart failure (HF) progression. However, the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and translational frontiers of senescence research in HF remain incompletely mapped.

Objective

This study mapped the global research landscape of cellular senescence in HF from 2005 to 2025 by integrating dual-database bibliometric analysis with BERTopic-based semantic topic modelling.

Methods

English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After field verification, standardization, and deduplication, 479 publications were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, SCImago Graphica, Pajek, Python, and Microsoft Excel were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses. PubMedBERT-based embeddings and BERTopic were applied to identify latent semantic themes from titles, abstracts, and keywords.

Results

Publications increased rapidly after 2020, with 336 papers published between 2020 and 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the corpus. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with the United States showing higher collaboration strength and accumulated citation counts within the analysed dataset. Co-citation analysis identified foundational studies in senescence biology, senolytics, cardiovascular ageing, and HF remodelling. Keyword evolution showed a shift from oxidative stress, cardiac stem/progenitor cell senescence, and vascular cell senescence toward inflammation, metabolic remodelling, biomarkers, HF phenotypes, and senotherapeutics. BERTopic identified 17 substantive topics, with Cardiac and Cardiovascular Aging as the largest theme, followed by Cardiac Fibrosis and Fibroblast Activation, SASP-related Cardiovascular Senescence, Cardiac Regeneration, and Doxorubicin Cardiotoxicity.

Conclusion

Bibliometric and semantic analyses indicate growing research interest in cell-type-specific senescence, inflammatory-fibrotic remodelling, HF phenotype heterogeneity, biomarkers, and senotherapeutics. These findings highlight opportunities for integrating mechanistic research with clinical investigation. Future studies should prioritize cell-specific senescence atlases, multidimensional biomarkers, comorbidity-aware HF stratification, and cautious evaluation of senotherapeutics in HF subgroups with evidence of senescence-associated pathology.

Rationale and objectives

Magnetic resonance diagnosis of pediatric acute appendicitis is highly accurate but may vary depending on reader training and subspecialty expertise. The study aims to compare the diagnostic performance of fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists and nonpediatric fellowship-trained emergency radiologists for non-contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) diagnosis of suspected pediatric acute appendicitis (AA).

Materials and methods

Retrospective, single-center study including 122 patients who underwent non-contrast-enhanced MRI for clinical concern of AA, following equivocal or inconclusive ultrasound. Reference standard based on clinical follow-up and surgical notes. Two fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists and two nonpediatric fellowship-trained emergency radiologists independently reviewed the examinations using a standardized yes/no case report form. Paired comparisons used McNemar's test. Predictive values are reported descriptively with 95% confidence intervals, with between-groups differences assessed using case-level bootstrap resampling. Appendix visualization was analyzed descriptively only.

Results

The cohort included 122 patients (63 male [51.6%], 59 female [48.4%]; median age 11 years, IQR 7-13 years, range 4-18 years), of whom 31 (25.4%) had pathology-confirmed AA. Sensitivity for MRI diagnosis of AA was similar between groups (fellowship-trained pediatric 87.1% [71.1-94.9] vs nonpediatric fellowship-trained 90.3% [75.1-96.7]; P = 1.00), with higher specificity among pediatric radiologists (97.8% [92.3-99.4] vs 84.6% [75.8-90.6]; P = 0.002). Specificity was also higher among pediatric radiologists for direct signs (98.9% [94.0-99.8] vs 86.8% [78.4-92.3]; P = 0.001) and for combined direct and indirect signs (98.9% vs 92.3%; P = 0.03), as was accuracy for MRI diagnosis of AA (95.1% [89.7-97.7] vs 86.1% [78.8-91.1]; P = 0.03) and for direct signs (94.3% vs 86.1%; P = 0.03). Positive predictive value was higher among pediatric radiologists for the diagnosis of AA, direct signs, and combined direct and indirect signs, reaching 96.2% (81.1-99.3) vs 68.4% (52.5-80.9) for direct signs (P < 0.001). Negative predictive value did not differ in any category. Interpretation time was longer for pediatric radiologists, with a median paired difference of 23.5 seconds (P = 0.04).

Conclusion

Fellowship-trained pediatric radiologists had higher specificity, positive predictive value, and accuracy than non-pediatric emergency radiologists for MRI diagnosis of suspected pediatric AA, with a small difference in interpretation time (median, 24 seconds). These findings, based on a limited number of readers, suggest differences in subspecialty expertise and aims and support further multicenter evaluation.

Background

Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents.

Objectives

This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT2prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR.

Methods

A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT2prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes. Sixty-four STEMI patients underwent CMR, including iT2prep-IR BOOST, clinical T2-STIR, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and T1/T2 mapping. The diagnostic performance of iT2prep-IR BOOST was evaluated against LGE and T2-STIR to assess myocardial infarction (MI), microvascular obstruction (MVO), and edema. Subgroup analyses further investigated the association between MVO detected by iT2prep-IR BOOST and left ventricular (LV) remodeling at 1-year follow-up.

Results

In 60 STEMI patients, the acquisition was completed in 7.2 ± 0.6min as a single free-breathing 3D whole-heart scan. Patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity for MVO (100.0% / 87.5%) and segmental MVO detection (95.8% / 97.8%). T2prep-IR BOOST yielded robust image contrast for MI comparable to LGE, while offering comparable edema visualization to T2-STIR. Volumetric and transmurality quantifications of MVO, MI, and edema showed excellent agreement with reference standards (all r > 0.90, p < 0.001), supported by significant biophysical correlations with native T1/T2 values (p < 0.001). Furthermore, in a 1-year follow-up cohort (n=51), baseline T2prep-IR BOOST-derived MVO volume was associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, showing significant correlations with both ΔLVEDVI (r = 0.305, p = 0.029) and ΔLVESVI (r = 0.293, p = 0.037).

Conclusions

In this preliminary single-center study, iT2prep-IR BOOST showed promising diagnostic performance and close quantitative agreement with conventional LGE and T2-STIR in stable STEMI patients. Further prospective validation in larger, independent, and more heterogeneous cohorts, including patients unable to undergo contrast-enhanced CMR, is required before this technique can be considered an alternative to standard LGE and T2-weighted sequences.

Background

Transanal surgery has advanced significantly since the introduction of transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) in 1983. The single-port (SP) robotic system marks the latest technological advancement in minimally invasive transanal surgery, combining single-site access with full robotic articulation through a single 25 mm port. This is the first video dynamic manuscript and 2nd document of a four-part SAGES Colorectal Committee series outlining the foundational application of SP technology in colorectal surgery, specifically transanal minimally invasive surgery (SP-TAMIS).

Methods

The SAGES Colorectal Committee SP Task Force performed a structured review of the da Vinci SP system, assessing platform features, instrumentation, and workflow considerations for transanal surgery. Task force members (subject matter experts with early experience with single-port robotic platforms) analyzed technical details, patient selection, operative workflows, and early outcomes. Representative procedural video-based techniques were detailed with emphasis on instrumentation, docking, and key operative steps specific to the SP transanal procedure.

Results

The SP platform appears to offer several technological advantages for transanal surgery: (1) natural hand-eye coordination in an inverted field, (2) enhanced visualization with an articulating cobra camera, and (3) a third arm for retraction and exposure. These features appear to improve precision, reduce collision risk and fatigue, and shorten operative time. Published early clinical data suggest low positive margin rates (≈ 4-5%) and acceptable morbidity for multiport robotic TAMIS/SP-TAMIS in selected patients. However, direct comparative evidence versus conventional TAMIS remains limited, and many comparisons are indirect across heterogeneous cohorts. Current limitations include high cost, limited distal reach, lack of dedicated energy devices, and learning curve. The learning curve appears to be shorter than for laparoscopic TAMIS. Peritoneal entry during full-thickness excision of upper rectal and anterior lesions is a recognized event in transanal surgery; the SP platform offers several features that may facilitate its management, though SP-specific incidence data are not yet available.

Conclusions

SME early experience with SP-TAMIS suggests that it can provide a safe, effective, and ergonomically superior method for local rectal excision. Mastery of this foundational application builds the skills needed for more complex SP colorectal procedures, with the potential for single-port robotics expansion into minimally invasive colorectal surgery through enhanced precision, reduced invasiveness, and improved surgeon ergonomics.

Background

PSMA PET/CT using 18F‑DCFPyL and 68Ga‑labelled tracers is central to prostate cancer staging, but 68Ga‑PSMA may show reduced sensitivity and quantitative accuracy, partly due to respiratory motion and lower spatial resolution. Device-based motion‑correction methods have limitations. Data‑driven gating (DDG) offers a hardware‑free alternative, though its impact on PSMA PET, especially 68Ga‑PSMA has not been systematically evaluated. To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of the DDG motion-correction method in 68Ga-PSMA and 18F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT, focusing on metastatic lymph node, lung, and bone lesions, and to assess its robustness across tracers.

Methods

This retrospective study included patients with biopsy‑proven prostate cancer who underwent 68Ga‑PSMA or 18F‑DCFPyL PSMA PET/CT for primary staging or biochemical recurrence and had metastatic disease. Motion correction was applied using the OncoFreeze AI™ data‑driven gating (OFAI‑DDG) method. Metastatic lesions were segmented semi‑automatically, and SUV metrics, image noise, and contrast‑to‑noise ratio were quantified by anatomical site in both OFAI-DDG and static images. Qualitative image quality was independently scored by two experienced readers. Statistical analyses included non‑parametric tests, Bland-Altman agreement, regression analyses, tracer comparison, and inter‑reader reliability assessment.

Results

After exclusions, 23 68Ga‑PSMA and 40 18F‑PSMA patients were analyzed, yielding 133 and 192 metastatic lesions, respectively. OFAI‑DDG reconstruction significantly increased SUVmean and SUVmax compared with static imaging for both tracers across bone, lymph node, and lung lesions (p < 0.0001), with the largest gains in lung lesions. CNR improved for most lesion types, and image noise was significantly reduced. Qualitative analysis showed better image quality, sharpness, and noise with OFAI‑DDG, with high inter‑reader agreement. OFAI‑DDG performance was robust across tracers and largely independent of lesion location.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates that OFAI‑DDG significantly improves PSMA PET/CT image quality and quantitative accuracy compared with standard static imaging. The improvements were observed for both 68Ga‑PSMA and 18F‑PSMA tracers, indicating tracer‑independent robustness. The OFAI‑DDG simplified the workflow and reduced time used for patient set-up, while enhancing lesion visualization and quantitative reliability without altering lesion detection, supporting its clinical value for metastatic prostate cancer imaging.
